newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vebacom extends network with Ruhrgas deal.
newsitem.headline: Vebacom extends network with Ruhrgas deal.

text.p: German telecommunications group Vebacom GmbH and utility Ruhrgas AG said on Monday they would cooperate in building a 4,000 km fibre optic communications network.
Under the agreement, Vebacom will be able to place cable along the gas pipelines of Ruhrgas and as many as 15 other utilities in Germany that were represented by Ruhrgas in the talks.

The deal also completes efforts by Vebacom to patch together a web of partnerships that would allow it to build a nation-wide communications backbone with total investment seen at around 600 million marks ($397 million).
Vebacom, a joint venture between Veba AG and Cable and Wireless, already has similar agreements with utilities Wintershall AG and PreussenElektra.
The company will use the network to offer corporate networks and services to wireless operators as well as public communications services when the German market is deregulated in 1998.
Vebacom's entire telecommunications transport network will be a 7,000 km fibre optic network based on so-called Synchronous Digital Hierarchy technology.
It will have a capacity of 2.5 gigabits, or 30,000 simultaneous conversations per pair of optical fibres. Each cable has 15-25 optical fibre pairs.
The network will connect Germany's 40 largest cities and will be operational in Hamburg, Hannover, Kassel and Frankfurt in January.
Vebacom has ordered switching equipment for the network from Lucent Technologies and Bosch Telecom.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097-150 ($ = 1.510 German Marks)
